comparison: Both evaluate the lack of PCFx impairments (C43, C44, C51). OpenEval finds the evidence robust based on statistical comparisons and validation against prior work. Peer reviewers accepted the data but found it 'surprising' and requested more detailed discussion of PCF role, indicating uncertainty about interpretation despite accepting the empirical findings.

Both address lesion validation (C27-C31). OpenEval finds converging histological evidence with quantitative measurements sufficient. Peer reviewers requested 'more detailed anatomical analyses' and better photomicrographs, stating 'it is difficult to determine this from Figure 1G,H,' indicating the evidence was insufficient for full support.

Both evaluate c-Fos findings (C46, C69, C70, C72). OpenEval finds quantitative c-Fos counting with appropriate statistics provides strong support. Peer reviewers acknowledged the correlation but expressed uncertainty about causation, noting 'the situation is likely to be rather complicated and other pathways could also be directly or indirectly involved.'

Both address spatial memory impairments in MTTx animals (C34, C35, C39). OpenEval finds statistical analyses and behavioral patterns support the claims. Peer reviewers explicitly affirmed these as 'interesting and important results' without questioning the behavioral data, showing strong agreement.

Both evaluate maze rotation effects (C41, C42). OpenEval finds behavioral data showing significant group differences after rotation well-supported. Peer reviewers described these effects as 'remarkable' and accepted the findings without challenge, demonstrating agreement.

Both address main conclusions about hippocampal-independent MB function (C3, C4, C7, C66, C67). OpenEval finds convergence of behavioral and c-Fos data provides strong support. Peer reviewers found results 'interesting and important' and acknowledged the 'dissociation of memory systems in the MB' without challenging main conclusions.

Both evaluate negative control findings (C73, C74, C57 overlap). OpenEval finds the pattern of selective effects strengthens specificity. Peer reviewers did not challenge these negative controls, with lack of comment suggesting implicit acceptance of the specificity findings.

Both address intact geometric discrimination performance (C59). OpenEval finds this provides evidence of task selectivity. Peer reviewers did not question this control finding, with lack of comment suggesting acceptance that lesion effects are selective rather than non-specific.

Both address hippocampal subfield analysis (C71). OpenEval finds the CA1-specific effects add anatomical specificity. Peer reviewers explicitly criticized the lack of detail, stating hippocampal regions were 'lumped together' with insufficient information about which neurons and layers showed c-Fos positivity.

Both address acetylcholinesterase staining control (C25). OpenEval includes this as part of converging histological validation. Peer reviewers did not question this methodological control, with lack of comment suggesting implicit acceptance of lesion specificity demonstration.

Both address c-Fos findings in PCFx animals and control regions (C5, C6). OpenEval finds no significant effects strengthen specificity. Peer reviewers acknowledged correlation between behavior and c-Fos but expressed uncertainty about causation and pathway complexity.

Both evaluate negative findings in supramammillary/septal regions (C57). OpenEval finds these provide evidence against alternative pathways though not definitive. Peer reviewers did not dispute the specificity of c-Fos changes to particular regions, suggesting acceptance.
